resolved.title: Armor
resolved.text: Place any armor piece tagged $(o)#magnetization:metal_armor$() in an electromagnet GUI to stamp it with a polarity. Vanilla iron / gold / chain / netherite qualify, along with all ten solid-material armor families, including late-game samarium–cobalt and neodymium.$(br)$(br)Wearing magnetized armor makes you a magnetizable entity — nearby fields pull you, and a held magnetized tool also vacuums dropped ferromagnetic items.

resolved.title: Tools
resolved.text: All ten solid-material families include swords, pickaxes, axes, shovels, and hoes. Each magnetized tool gets a signature ability on top of the shared item-vacuum:$(br)$(li)$(l)Sword$() — yank nearby entities toward you on hit.$(li)$(l)Pickaxe$() — rip neighbouring ferromagnetic ore on break.$(li)$(l)Axe$() — pulse-knockback enemies on attack.$(li)$(l)Shovel$() — chance to pan magnetite nuggets when digging.$(li)$(l)Hoe$() — dowsing ping reveals ferromagnetic blocks nearby.$(br)$(br)Magnetized neodymium tools contribute twice the personal harvesting pull of other tiers.

resolved.title: Full Item List
resolved.text: $(l)Maghemite tier$() — $(o)maghemite_sword$() / $(o)maghemite_pickaxe$() / $(o)maghemite_axe$() / $(o)maghemite_shovel$() / $(o)maghemite_hoe$() / $(o)maghemite_helmet$() / $(o)maghemite_chestplate$() / $(o)maghemite_leggings$() / $(o)maghemite_boots$() / $(o)maghemite_horse_armor$()$(br)$(br)$(l)Magnetite tier$() — $(o)magnetite_sword$() / $(o)magnetite_pickaxe$() / $(o)magnetite_axe$() / $(o)magnetite_shovel$() / $(o)magnetite_hoe$() / $(o)magnetite_helmet$() / $(o)magnetite_chestplate$() / $(o)magnetite_leggings$() / $(o)magnetite_boots$() / $(o)magnetite_horse_armor$()$(br)$(br)$(l)Ferromagnetic tier$() — $(o)ferromagnetic_sword$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_pickaxe$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_axe$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_shovel$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_hoe$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_helmet$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_chestplate$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_leggings$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_boots$() / $(o)ferromagnetic_horse_armor$()

resolved.title: More Complete Sets
resolved.text: Gallium, lithium, pyrrhotite, hematite, and titanomagnetite follow the same complete pattern as the original families. Each has a sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots, horse armor, refined storage block, and — where a raw material exists — a raw storage block. MR-fluid gear is the exception: it is stored as fluid and hardens in fields instead of being pulled.

resolved.title: Horse Armor
resolved.text: Horse body armor counts as armor for magnetism purposes — equip a horse with magnetite or ferromagnetic horse armor and the horse becomes a magnetizable entity. Stamp polarity in any electromagnet GUI just like wearable armor. Magnetite horse armor matches iron in defense; ferromagnetic matches diamond.

resolved.title: Maghemite Horse Armor
resolved.text: 7 maghemite ingots in a U-shape. Below iron in defense — fits the rusted-magnetite flavour. Still tagged for magnetism so a stamped horse drifts in fields.

resolved.title: Magnetite Horse Armor
resolved.text: 7 ingots in a U-shape. Iron-tier protection (armor 5) for your horse.

resolved.title: Ferromagnetic Horse Armor
resolved.text: Same U-shape with ferromagnetic ingots. Diamond-tier protection (armor 11).

resolved.title: Magnetic Anomaly
resolved.text: Rare cold/dry inland biome. Compasses spin wildly inside. Fields get a $(l)1.5×$() strength bonus here — build labs and arena PvP zones here for amped effects.$(br)$(br)$(o)/magnetization tp anomaly$() to scout.

resolved.title: Petrified Forest
resolved.text: Rare biome covered in petrified wood. Lightning strikes on petrified logs may magnetize the strike point. Petrified wood is weakly ferromagnetic.$(br)$(br)$(o)/magnetization tp petrified_forest$() to scout.
Points at the nearest active emitter in range. Shift+right-click for an entity-locked variant. Curios-slot compatible.
Right-click an attractive emitter to zip toward it. Default range $(l)24 blocks$(). Curios-slot compatible.

resolved.title: Ships & Portals
resolved.text: Create: AeroPortals transfers preserve ship magnetic state, inventories, connected child craft, constraints, and installed or carried Railgun Remotes. Immersive Portals can project magnetic fields through a reachable portal aperture, transforming direction and scale while preventing recursive or duplicate force. Both integrations activate only when their mods are installed.

resolved.title: Coasters, Trains & Tracks
resolved.text: Create: Coasters Simulated carts react to magnetic fields like ships, even while loose; only rail-engaged coaster structures are recognized by the Structural Inducer. Track Styles and Coasters Extras preserve that parent cart behavior. A Magnetization field can power Coasters: Magnetized anchors instead of redstone, while Coasters: Engineered gains a Magnetic Alloy Linear Motor recipe. Create: Tracks components contribute vehicle susceptibility. Steam 'n' Rails applies force once to the shared train along its rail.

resolved.title: Create Addons
resolved.text: Create: Big Cannons projectiles can react to fields without magnetizing cannon carriages or gas. EMP Flux Charges permanently disable guidance computers on intersecting CBC Aeronautics Missiles, without changing their propulsion, payloads, or fuzes. Copycats inherit susceptibility from their copied material. Create: Cosmonautics accepts Magnetization Hydrogen as rocket fuel and gains magnetic spacecraft recipes. Create: New Age, Crafts & Additions, Diesel Generators, Enchantment Industry, and other supported addons receive curated material roles.

resolved.title: Materials & Fuels
resolved.text: Common $(o)c:$() tags make supported metals, magnetic alloy plates, and Lithium interchangeable. TFMG magnets work in Magnetization's magnet-slot machines, and its electrical machines have curated magnetic/conductive physics roles. TFMG can mix Ferrofluid with Lubrication Oil, cast Gallium/Lithium, blast Magnetite or Hematite into steel, and use Permanent Magnets in electrical recipes. Molten Steel is an MHD working fluid. The powered Polarizer field is opt-in under $(o)compat.tfmgPolarizerFieldEnabled$().

resolved.title: HUDs & Recipe Viewers
resolved.text: Create goggles, Jade, WTHIT, and The One Probe show live emitter and machine status. On Sable craft, Sable owns sublevel targeting while Magnetization supplies one set of field/machine lines. JEI, REI, and EMI expose recipes and magnetic-material information. Just Enough Resources, a JEI add-on, adds 28 synchronized charts for all ore variants and natural resources. Create's Ponder adds animated setup scenes for multiblocks, machines, rare-earth magnets, and supported addon behavior.

resolved.title: Compatibility Controls
resolved.text: Optional behavior integrations and informational viewers each have a master switch under $(l)Cross-Mod Compatibility$(), including AeroPortals, Immersive Portals, Copycats+, Curios, TFMG, Cosmonautics, Simulated Coasters, Coasters: Magnetized, Coasters: Engineered, CBC Aeronautics Missiles, Steam 'n' Rails, Patchouli, JER, Jade, WTHIT, The One Probe, JEI, REI, and EMI. Sub-feature and recipe controls remain available beneath their master. Recipe changes take effect after resources reload or restart. Static tags remain datapack-controlled.

resolved.title: Extra Golems Reborn
resolved.text: Reborn 21.1.0.1 is an optional, unofficial port. Raw iron/gold/copper, gold, netherite, ancient debris and all copper oxidation/waxing variants react to physical emitters and magnetic golems. Wood, stone and nether brick have no automatic body response; magnetic armor can still react.$(br2)The server controls $(o)compat.extraGolemsRebornCompatEnabled$() and $(o)compat.extraGolemsRebornMaterials$(). Changes apply next tick after config reload. Explicit entity tags act independently; the unmoveable tag always wins.

resolved.title: Compatibility Evidence
resolved.text: The README links the versioned compatibility matrix and its tests. Missing optional tag entries are harmless to loading but do not prove support.$(br2)Alex’s Caves support targets the unofficial 1.21.1 port; Bosses of Mass Destruction targets its NeoForge port. Legacy Extra Golems, Modular Golems and Quark entity guesses were removed. Shared material tags remain useful where populated. Checks cover material-aware golem adapters, native lightning, storage across a server restart, and cannon/bellows workflows. Moving pulley payloads still fail during ship splitting. See the matrix for tested scope.

resolved.title: Magnetics Server Fix
resolved.text: Create: Magnetics 0.0.4-alpha has an upstream dedicated-server crash caused by loading client sound classes.$(br2)Magnetization includes a default-off workaround: set $(o)compat.createMagneticsServerCrashWorkaround$() to $(o)true$() in $(o)config/magnetization-common.toml$() before starting the server. A full server restart is required.$(br2)It applies only to that version on dedicated servers. Client sounds and magnetic gameplay are unchanged.

resolved.title: Material-aware creatures
resolved.text: $(thing)Modular Golems 3.1.43$() use their current parts’ crafting ingredients and our magnetic material rules. $(thing)Quark 4.1-485$() Toretoises respond while carrying iron or copper ore; harvested shells do not. Each body counts once, and magnetic armor can still contribute. Both optional adapters default on in server config. Explicit entity tags can opt in an entire type even when its adapter is disabled.

resolved.title: Native lightning
resolved.text: $(thing)Alex’s Caves Unofficial Port 2.0.10$() Tesla Bulbs stamp eligible equipment and can petrify logs. $(thing)Magnetron punches and slams$() remain physical and non-LIRM by default. The experimental $(thing)Magnetron melee LIRM$() server option adds those effects after successful hits. Both compatibility and LIRM masters apply; config reload takes effect. Cosmetic bolts, including Ur-Ghast effects, leave logs and ground fields unchanged.

resolved.title: Piloted aircraft
resolved.text: $(thing)Immersive Aircraft 1.5.2$() and $(thing)Aviator Dreams Reloaded 1.2.7$() simulate piloted flight on the client. Our fields add magnetic impulses while native controls remain active. The server’s $(thing)Piloted Aircraft Magnetic Speed Limit$() defaults to 1 block per tick for added acceleration. Existing faster native speed is preserved; magnetic braking and deflection still work. Config reload changes subsequent impulses.

resolved.title: Where Settings Live
resolved.text: Player-facing, gameplay, compatibility, and worldgen settings live in the global $(o)magnetization-common.toml$(), editable from the Mods screen before opening a world. Admin GUI limits and command permissions live in the per-world server config. Dedicated-server owners edit the server's files; its gameplay values are authoritative.

resolved.title: Disabling Content
resolved.text: Use $(o)content.disabledBlocks$() and $(o)content.disabledItems$() to soft-disable registry paths without removing them from old saves. Example: $(o)disabledBlocks = ["dipole_electromagnet"]$(). Disabled blocks are inert, hidden from the creative tab, skip their GUI, and have their recipes removed. Existing placements remain safely in the world.

resolved.title: Multiplayer Authority
resolved.text: When joining a server, Magnetization synchronizes its authoritative COMMON gameplay settings to the client so GUIs, HUD meters, capacities, and tooltips match server behavior. The client's local values are restored after disconnect. If a display disagrees, reconnect before changing the client's file.

resolved.title: Hunt the Sky-Fall
resolved.text: A Field Compass with a meteorite fragment infused into the casing. The needle scans for the nearest active $(l)meteorite_core$() within 512 blocks and points to it. Fully-decayed meteorites are invisible to the compass — only cores still emitting are tracked.$(br)$(br)Bonus: unlike the Field Compass, the Cosmic Compass is $(l)not$() scrambled by the Magnetic Anomaly biome. Meteorite signals read clean above the biome's flux noise.
Field Compass + 1 Meteorite Fragment (shapeless).

Heavy water — water whose hydrogen is the heavier $(l)deuterium$() isotope. Craft it from an empty bucket + glowstone dust, or smelt/blast a water bucket. It behaves like water (a touch denser and darker) and feeds the Deuterium Cell recipe, Tritium breeding, and Fusion Thruster.

$(l)Pyrolytic Carbon$() (4 charcoal) is strongly diamagnetic. Dropped within a magnetic field it's repelled by $(l)both$() poles — pushed away with its motion damped — so it settles into a stable hover above a magnet instead of being pulled in. Real diamagnetic levitation.

Press four wafers into a $(l)Diamagnetic Block$(). Build it into a Sable craft and the whole ship turns diamagnetic — $(l)repelled by both poles$() of any field, regardless of polarity (the opposite of a ferromagnetic hull). Add a $(l)Polarity Inverter$() to the ship to flip it to $(l)attracted$() to both poles instead. (Server config can swap the default.)

resolved.title: Alternative power
resolved.text: Every tunable redstone emitter — Electromagnet, Dipole Electromagnet, Magnetic Anchor, Repulsor Coil, Tractor Beam, Magnetic Excavator, and Structural Inducer — also accepts $(l)FE/RF$() from any energy-providing mod. No specific energy-mod dependency is needed; FE is built into NeoForge.

resolved.title: How it works
resolved.text: Each emitter has an internal $(l)50,000 FE$() buffer (default). Connect any FE source — wires, cables, generators — and the buffer fills.$(br)$(br)$(l)Redstone takes priority$(): if the emitter is receiving a redstone signal, that drives it for free. Without redstone, the emitter consumes $(l)10 FE/tick$() from its buffer while emitting. The GUI's right-side bar shows current fill and active source.

resolved.title: Admin toggles
resolved.text: Server owners can allow either source for field emitters and Railgun Emitters via $(o)compat.allowRedstonePower$() and $(o)compat.allowEnergyPower$(). These compatibility toggles do not control propulsion machines; use $(o)propulsion.allowRedstoneThrustPower$() for propulsion. Enable $(o)compat.requireRedstoneAndEnergy$() to require a signal and buffered FE together; without the signal, no FE is burned. Set both source toggles on and require-both off for the default either-or behavior.

resolved.title: Analog Redstone
resolved.text: The seven $(o)compat.analogRedstone*$() toggles are independent and off by default. Enable one to make that emitter's force follow signal strength: level 1 is WEAK (200 N), level 15 is EXTREME (8,000 N), with geometric steps between. The configured tier still controls range; goggles and HUDs show the throttled force.

A black, water-like magnetic liquid. Generates naturally $(l)only in the Magnetic Anomaly biome$() (its water bodies are ferrofluid); otherwise craft a bucket from an $(l)empty bucket + 2 raw magnetite$(). Plain ferrofluid is $(l)field-immune$() — it sits still and reacts to nothing on its own.

Place it at the bottom of a drop: anyone wearing $(l)metallic armor$() who lands on it has their fall completely arrested — zero fall damage from any height. Without metallic armor (the conductor the field grips), it's a normal landing.

resolved.title: Antiferromagnetic Dampener
resolved.text: A full block of hematite is a $(l)passive dampener$(). It emits no field of its own — α-Fe₂O₃ is antiferromagnetic, every dipole pair cancels — but placed next to any active emitter, each adjacent hematite face drops the emitter's effective strength tier by one step.

resolved.title: Stacking Dampeners
resolved.text: Strength steps down sequentially: $(br)$(br)EXTREME $(o)→$() STRONG $(o)→$() WEAK $(br)$(br)WEAK is the clamp floor — adding more hematite faces past that point has no further effect. Use it to throttle an over-powered emitter without rewiring its GUI, or to surround a polarity-locked emitter with a soft falloff zone.

resolved.title: Polarity Lock
resolved.text: A hematite-cored polarizer disc that locks an emitter's polarity in place. Once installed, no Polarity Inverter, anomaly biome flux, or other passing field can flip the locked emitter's polarity — it stays exactly where you set it.
1 hematite ingot + 1 magnetic plate (shapeless).

resolved.title: How to Use
resolved.text: The polarizer itself carries a target polarity (NORTH by default).$(br)$(br)$(l)Right-click in air$() — toggle the polarizer between NORTH and SOUTH.$(br)$(l)Shift + right-click an emitter$() — install the polarizer's current polarity as a lock on that emitter, or remove an existing lock if one is already there.$(br)$(br)Plain right-click on an emitter is intentionally untouched — that still does the block's normal action (rotate, polarity flip, open GUI). All lock gestures live on sneak. The polarizer is reusable — installing or removing a lock doesn't consume it, and the lock survives world reloads.

resolved.title: Portable Field Memory
resolved.text: Refined titanomagnetite suspended in an ender-pearl matrix gives you a hand-held version of the titanomagnetite block's field-recording trick. Capture any emitter's exact configuration, walk it across the map, and project the same config onto another emitter — no manual re-tuning.
1 ender pearl in the centre, 4 titanomagnetite ingots in a plus-shape.

resolved.title: How to Use
resolved.text: $(l)Shift + right-click an active emitter$() while the module is empty to capture its strength, polarity, and range. The tooltip then shows what type of emitter the imprint was taken from.$(br)$(br)$(l)Shift + right-click another emitter$() while the module is filled to project the captured preset onto it. Reusable indefinitely — no charges to track.$(br)$(br)$(l)Right-click in air$() to clear a filled imprint so you can capture a new source. Plain right-click on an emitter is intentionally left alone — that still does the block's normal action (rotate, polarity flip, open GUI). All imprint gestures live on sneak.$(br)$(br)The target emitter clamps projected values to its own GUI ceilings. If you captured an Electromagnet at EXTREME and project onto a Repulsor Coil with a lower max strength, the Repulsor lands at its own ceiling instead of being rejected. Cross-type projection works freely — the tooltip's source line lets you avoid accidental mismatches.

resolved.title: Temporary magnetization
resolved.text: A lightning strike on a player wearing metal armor / tools imparts a $(l)temporary$() magnetization (LIRM). The polarity stamp decays linearly over 20 minutes, then auto-clears.$(br)$(br)Free magnetism — but watch the timer. Permanent stamps via the Electromagnet GUI do not decay.

The $(l)Homopolar Motor$() and $(l)MHD Jet$() can $(o)consume$() their installed magnet while running. Magnet burning is disabled by default; enable $(l)Propulsion → Magnet-Slot Machines Burn Magnets$() to turn it on. When enabled, burn time scales with the magnet's $(l)strength$() and $(l)quantity$(): a storage block lasts by far the longest (it holds 9 units), a bare weak ore is the floor.$(br2)Stronger magnets both output more $(o)and$() last longer. Leave the setting off when magnets should remain permanent inputs.

Anvils cast from our metals — full vanilla anvil behaviour, but $(l)self-dampened$() (no clang) with per-metal durability. Magnetite/maghemite/hematite are convenient-but-degrading; $(l)Titanomagnetite never degrades$() — the only metal that beats a vanilla anvil + dampener.

resolved.title: Rail-Riding the Sky
resolved.text: A vanilla elytra reforged with ferromagnetic plate and magnetic_plate. Wears in the chest slot like the original; glides like the original. The difference appears in flight: while gliding, the wearer's field-susceptibility multiplies $(4 4×)$, so passing emitters tug them harder than they would on foot.
Vanilla elytra in the centre, magnetic plate above, ferromagnetic ingots in the corners + bottom.

resolved.title: Surf the Fields
resolved.text: Build a line of permanent magnets or powered emitters along a flight corridor and the elytra wearer can $(l)rail-ride$() between them — NORTH emitters pull, SOUTH emitters push. Stamp the elytra (and any other equipped armor) with a chosen polarity in the electromagnet GUI to decide which emitters attract and which repel.$(br)$(br)Skilled pilots can chain attractive and repulsive emitters to launch themselves cross-map without rockets. Combine with the Imprint Module to deploy matched-config emitter chains quickly. Repair using ferromagnetic ingots.

A thin magnetic plate that mounts on any face and displays one item, tool, or armor piece. Right-click with an item to insert one. Power the frame with redstone or FE to spin it; empty-hand right-click or a wrench cycles the spin direction. Sneak + empty-hand removes the item.

Drop a ferrofluid bucket in the $(l)electromagnet GUI$() and pick a pole to magnetize it. Pour it out and it's a $(l)flowing fluid that also emits a weak field$(), pulling items and ships with that polarity. Magnetized fluid flowing into plain ferrofluid converts it — $(l)magnetization takes priority$().

Magnetic-metal boots that $(l)auto-save you from any fall$() (costing a little durability per save). Uniquely, they're $(l)inert to fields$() — never yanked by emitters — until you magnetize them in the electromagnet GUI, after which they react like other magnetized gear.

resolved.title: Visitors From Above
resolved.text: Rare iron-nickel cores that survive atmospheric entry and bury themselves on the surface, leaving behind a carved $(l)impact crater$() of magnetite, raw_magnetite, and petrified_wood. The core sits at the bowl's centre. Each one emits a powerful magnetic field that decays over ~10 in-game minutes after generation — fresh meteorites pulse at $(l)EXTREME$() strength, faded ones $(l)WEAK$(), and fully-decayed ones go inert.

$(l)Meteorite Core$() $(br)$(br)Worldgen-only — extremely rare overworld surface block embedded in a carved crater. Search for one with a $(l)Cosmic Compass$() (long-range) or a field compass (short-range); the needle will track the decaying signal until it fully fades. Use a ferromagnetic item to right-click and recharge.

resolved.title: Maintaining a Core
resolved.text: Right-click a meteorite core with any ferromagnetic item (magnetite, hematite, raw_iron, etc.) to consume that item and reset the decay timer to full charge. This lets a player keep a found meteorite as a permanent power source — at the cost of an ongoing magnetic-material feed.

resolved.title: Cross-Mod: AE2 Meteors
resolved.text: If $(l)Applied Energistics 2$() is installed, every AE2 meteor structure also emits a decaying magnetic field at its centre — same decay curve as a native meteorite_core, but with no extra block placed (AE2's sky_stone is undisturbed). A Cosmic Compass will track AE2 meteors right alongside native ones. Server owners can disable this in config: $(l)compat.ae2MeteoriteHookEnabled = false$().

Rare reagent dropped (1–3 per break) when you mine a $(l)meteorite_core$(). Pre-magnetised at the molecular level — every fragment carries traces of the parent meteorite's decaying field. Used as a shortcut catalyst in two recipes:

resolved.title: Cosmic Ferromagnetic Recipe
resolved.text: 1 fragment + 4 magnetite (plus-shape) → 8 ferromagnetic ingots. Skips the lodestone-core gating of the standard recipe; per-fragment yield is higher but you need to actually find a meteorite first.

resolved.title: Cosmic Lodestone Recipe
resolved.text: 1 fragment + 1 magnetic_plate (shapeless) → 4 lodestone cores. The fragment substitutes for the 8-plate spiral of the standard recipe — flavoured as the meteorite already carrying the field.

resolved.title: Cultivating the Sky-Fall
resolved.text: A seed-form of the $(l)meteorite_core$(). Plant one anywhere a sapling could go, leave it alone for about 30 in-game minutes, and it $(l)matures$() into a freshly-charged Meteorite Core with a full EXTREME-strength field.$(br)$(br)Unlike the Core itself, the Sapling drops back to inventory if broken — useful if you planted it in a bad spot.
Craft a sapling from one Meteorite Fragment cradled in four raw magnetite.

$(l)Meteorite Sapling$()$(br)$(br)Place on any solid block; it grows on its own as long as the chunk stays loaded. No light, water, or sky access required — the sapling consumes its own ferromagnetic mass.

Iron-light, flexible armor infused with magnetorheological fluid. Inside a $(l)magnetic field$() it stays permanently rigid — shrugging off $(l)nearly all damage$() (full set ≈ 95%) and it's never pulled by the field. Out of a field it instead snaps rigid the instant a $(l)kinetic hit$() lands (physical/fall/blast), scaling with pieces worn (≈ 90%). Made by infusing iron armor with MR fluid.

An iron-particle smart fluid. It flows like a liquid, but a $(l)redstone signal$() or $(l)magnetic field$() instantly stiffens it into $(l)Hardened MR Fluid$() — a solid block you can walk on. Remove both activations and it melts back. Build wired or field-toggled bridges, gates, and walkways.

An iron-golem-like guardian bodied in magnetorheological fluid. Crafted as a $(l)spawn egg$() (four MR fluid buckets around a carved pumpkin) since you can't stack a fluid into a multiblock. While fluid it soaks 30% of damage and can be knocked back; inside a $(l)magnetic field$() it locks rigid, soaking 92% and becoming immovable. Repair it with an MR Fluid Bucket, not iron. Create goggles, Jade, WTHIT, and The One Probe show its live state. Server owners can disable its recipe, egg, and material behavior with $(o)content.mrFluidGolemEnabled$().
A dowsing rod for $(l)metallic ore veins$() — it points to the nearest one. Combine it with a specific metallic ore in an anvil to $(l)tune$() it to track only that ore instead of any.

resolved.title: Heat-Activated Emitter
resolved.text: A full block of pyrrhotite is a $(l)heat-activated magnetic emitter$(). On its own it's inert; place a heat source on any of its six faces and the lattice's iron sulfide dipoles align, broadcasting a $(l)NORTH$()-polarity omnidirectional field whose strength rises with the heat level.

resolved.title: Heat → Strength
resolved.text: Create's $(l)Blaze Burner$() is the canonical heat source; mapping is: $(br)$(br)$(l)Smouldering$() / $(l)Fading$() → WEAK $(br)$(l)Kindled$() → STRONG $(br)$(l)Seething$() → EXTREME $(br)$(br)No adjacent heat = no field. To flip polarity, stack a $(l)Polarity Inverter$() next to the block.

resolved.title: Heat Bridging
resolved.text: Direct adjacency works, but most setups use a $(l)Pyrrhotite Catalyst$() to bridge heat across a few blocks — see the Catalyst entry. Mixed-tier Catalyst networks stack (largest reach in range wins). Tooltip on the block always reports the current observed heat tier so you can debug a chain visually.

resolved.title: Heat Bridge
resolved.text: Normally a pyrrhotite block only sees heat on its six $(o)directly adjacent$() faces — touch a blaze burner to one face, the block lights up; one block away, nothing.$(br)$(br)A $(l)Pyrrhotite Catalyst$() relays heat across distance. Touch any heat source to one of the Catalyst's faces, and every pyrrhotite block within the Catalyst's $(l)transmit radius$() (3, 5, or 7 blocks depending on tier) reads that same heat as if it were touching the source itself.

resolved.title: What counts as heat
resolved.text: The Catalyst forwards any heat source the pyrrhotite reactor would normally accept directly:$(br)$(li)Create blaze burner — full heat scale$(li)Lava — SEETHING$(li)Fire / soul fire / magma block — KINDLED$(li)Lit campfire / soul campfire — SMOULDERING$(br)$(br)Hover the Catalyst to see what heat tier it's currently bridging.

resolved.title: Chaining Catalysts
resolved.text: Catalysts compose freely. Place a row of them and each one independently transmits heat to any pyrrhotite within its own radius — so a single blaze burner can drive a string of pyrrhotite reactors along a long Catalyst spine. Mixed tiers stack naturally: if a pyrrhotite block falls within two Catalysts' radii, the larger one wins.

resolved.title: Catalyst Tiers
resolved.text: Three tiers ship: $(l)Basic$() reaches 3 blocks, $(l)Enhanced$() 5, and $(l)Cosmic$() 7. Each tier scans for pyrrhotite within its own radius — mixed-tier networks stack naturally (the largest reach in range wins). Recipes use progressively rarer reagents: Enhanced layers in netherite scrap, Cosmic uses meteorite fragments.
Basic — 3-block transmit radius.
Enhanced — 5-block radius.
Cosmic — 7-block radius.
Hand-held conical repulsor. Right-click to fire a single pulse in your look direction. Cooldown-gated like the Magnetic Grapple — no fuel.

resolved.title: Three effects per shot
resolved.text: $(li)$(l)Ships$() in the cone get pushed away.$(li)$(l)Magnetized entities$() (mobs in magnetized armor, or carrying the Magnetized effect) get knockback.$(li)$(l)Dropped items and falling blocks$() get nudged out of the cone — defensive crowd-clearing trick.

resolved.title: Self-recoil & curios
resolved.text: If your shot lands on a $(l)magnetic emitter block$() (lodestone, electromagnet, permanent magnet, etc.), you get $(l)kicked back$() along the inverse of your aim — closer magnet = harder push. The headline traversal trick: aim down at a lodestone to launch yourself upward and backward.$(br)$(br)Curios-compatible: drop the gun in a charm slot and bind $(o)Use Repulsor Gun$() under $(l)Options → Controls → Key Binds → Magnetization$().
One Magnetic Plate, one Lodestone Core, one Ferromagnetic Ingot, and three iron ingots. The plate shapes the cone, the core anchors the field, the ingot stiffens the recoil bracket.

resolved.title: Paleomagnetic Record
resolved.text: A full block of titanomagnetite is a $(l)field recorder$(). Place it within a few blocks of any active emitter; on its next tick it captures the strongest neighbouring field (strength, polarity, shape) into its block-entity and starts re-emitting that field from its own position.$(br)$(br)Remove the source emitter and the titanomagnetite keeps emitting indefinitely. Re-expose to a stronger field to overwrite the imprint. The record persists across world reloads and server restarts.

resolved.title: Reading & Resetting
resolved.text: Hover the block: the tooltip shows $(l)Recorded: STRONG NORTH$() (or similar) once a field has been captured, or an empty-state hint before that. The block needs $(l)no power$() — its emission is passive, driven by the captured imprint.$(br)$(br)Break and replace the block to wipe the imprint. For a portable version, craft an $(l)Imprint Module$() — same paleomagnetic trick, hand-held.

The Tokamak is a flat, expandable fusion reactor. A complete structure accepts Deuterium, Tritium, and Helium-3 fuel cells; larger structures linearly increase FE capacity, generation, output, and cooling-water storage. The following pages show the required solid-core layout and where automation connects.

resolved.title: Solid-Core Layout
resolved.text: Build the whole reactor in $(l)one horizontal layer$(). Make an odd square with a one-block $(l)Confinement Coil$() perimeter, then fill $(l)every$() interior position with Reactor Cores. A hollow interior or any wrong/missing block invalidates it.$(br2)$(l)3x3:$() 8 coils + 1 core$(br)$(l)5x5:$() 16 coils + 9 cores$(br)$(l)7x7:$() 24 coils + 25 cores$(br2)In general, edge N needs 4N-4 coils and (N-2)^2 cores, up to the configured maximum.

resolved.title: Master & Connections
resolved.text: The exact center core is the sole master; follower cores do not create extra reactors. Right-click or automate fuel into $(l)any core$() to reach the shared slot. FE can be extracted from any core or any perimeter coil. Vanilla water and tagged coolant buckets work by hand, hopper, Create funnel, or arm; Create fluid pipes can feed coolant through any core or perimeter coil. All cores mirror the active glow.$(br2)Breaking any required core or coil stops fusion. Create goggles and supported HUDs show size, multiplier, fuel, cooling, and validity.

resolved.title: Optional Cooling
resolved.text: The reactor keeps its previous output with an empty coolant tank. $(l)Water$() is the baseline; $(l)Deuterium Oxide$() is modestly better, $(l)liquid Gallium$() is the high-efficiency liquid-metal option, and fluids tagged $(o)c:cooling_fluid$() use the tagged curve. TFMG Cooling Fluid also requires $(o)compat.tfmgCoolingFluidEnabled$(). Better coolant is consumed more slowly and raises the configured power and fuel-life bonuses. The tank and base cost scale with ring size. The GUI/HUD distinguishes Dry, Ready, and Active cooling.

resolved.title: Anomalous Bedrock
resolved.text: Inside the Anomaly biome the very stone is iron-rich, faintly green from oxidised iron veining. The biome's surface is paved in $(l)anomaly stone$() and $(l)magnetic gravel$() — mine, smelt, and build with the full vanilla-stone family of variants.

$(l)Anomaly Stone$()$(br)$(br)Stone variant with iron-oxide veining baked in. Drops cobbled when mined; silk-touch keeps the smooth form. Smelt cobbled back into smooth in a furnace, exactly like vanilla.
$(l)Cobbled Anomaly Stone$()$(br)$(br)The default mining result. Crafts into stairs, slabs, and walls (recipes follow) and can be stonecut for 1:1 yield.

$(l)Magnetic Gravel$()$(br)$(br)Iron-flecked dark gravel. Falls under gravity like normal gravel, and emitters lightly attract it. Vanilla flint is replaced by a small chance of $(l)raw magnetite$() (5%) or $(l)raw maghemite$() (3%) when mined.$(br)$(br)$(o)Worldgen$(): bulk of the Anomaly surface is magnetic gravel, plus very sparse patches in vanilla overworld biomes (~1-in-24 chunks) so survival players who never reach an Anomaly biome can still find a small supply. Disable via $(o)magneticGravelInVanillaBiomes = false$() in the server config.

Alloy ingot that mixes magnetite with iron + lodestone for endgame-tier recipes. Used in the top-tier armor + tools, the Repulsor Gun, Magnetic Grapple, and most field-shaping blocks. Tagged $(o)#magnetization:ferromagnetic$() so it's pulled by attractive fields.

resolved.title: Crafting
resolved.text: 1 lodestone_core in the centre, magnetite ingots on the four edges, iron ingots on the four corners → 3 ferromagnetic ingots. Cheaper shortcut: $(l)1 meteorite_fragment + 4 magnetite$() (plus-shape) → 8 ferromagnetic ingots, but requires a meteorite hunt first.

resolved.title: Magnetism, the short version
resolved.text: Every block in this addon either $(l)emits a magnetic field$() or $(l)responds to one$(). Fields have a $(6)polarity$() ($(3)NORTH$() or $(c)SOUTH$()), a strength tier ($(o)WEAK→EXTREME$()), and a shape (omnidirectional, directional, conical).$(br)Like polarities $(c)repel$(); opposite polarities $(3)attract$(). That's the entire rule.

resolved.title: Where forces apply
resolved.text: Fields push or pull:$(br)$(li)$(l)Sable sub-levels$() — Create: Aeronautics ships intersecting the field. Big ships rotate naturally because closer ends feel stronger pull.$(li)$(l)Magnetizable entities$() — iron golems, undead mobs, ferromagnetic item drops, players in metal armor.$(br)$(br)Onboard-only setups produce zero net thrust — internal forces cancel, just like real physics. To propel a ship, build $(o)between$() the world and the ship.

resolved.title: Beyond Magnetite
resolved.text: Magnetite is the headline iron-oxide ore, but the family runs deeper: $(l)maghemite$() (oxidised surface variant), $(l)pyrrhotite$() (heat-activated iron sulfide), $(l)hematite$() (antiferromagnetic dampener), and $(l)titanomagnetite$() (rare deep-rock field recorder).$(br)$(br)All four smelt into useful ingots and are tagged for standard emitter pulls. Their block mechanics and specialist items are documented in the Advanced category.

$(l)Maghemite$() $(br)$(br)Reddish iron(III) oxide that forms when magnetite weathers. Drops $(l)raw maghemite$() from ore; smelt for a maghemite ingot. Surface-y Y-band (40..120). Also where your hoarded magnetite ends up — see $(l)oxidation decay$().
$(l)Pyrrhotite$() $(br)$(br)Bronze-tinted iron sulfide. Block form is a $(l)heat-activated emitter$() — see the Pyrrhotite Block entry. Mid-depths Y-band (-32..48).
$(l)Hematite$() $(br)$(br)Dark-red α-Fe₂O₃. Antiferromagnetic — block form is a $(l)field dampener$() (see the Hematite Block entry). Broad Y-band (-40..96). Ingots also craft into red dye.
$(l)Titanomagnetite$() $(br)$(br)Iron-titanium oxide that records the last magnetic field it was exposed to and re-emits it. See the Titanomagnetite Block entry. Scarce deep-rock spawn (-64..-8).

resolved.title: Oxidation Decay
resolved.text: Inventory oxidation is $(l)optional and disabled by default$(). When $(o)content.magnetiteOxidationEnabled$() is enabled, loose $(l)raw magnetite$() and $(l)magnetite ingots$() gradually convert in place to their maghemite equivalents. The default delay is one Minecraft week (7 days), controlled by $(o)content.magnetiteOxidationTicks$().$(br)$(br)A tooltip shows the remaining percentage. Block forms are exempt, and maghemite does not decay further.

resolved.title: Block + Item Variants
resolved.text: Each ore family ships in the standard set:$(br)$(li)$(o)maghemite_ore$() / $(o)deepslate_maghemite_ore$() / $(o)maghemite_block$() / $(o)raw_maghemite_block$()$(li)$(o)pyrrhotite_ore$() / $(o)deepslate_pyrrhotite_ore$() / $(o)pyrrhotite_block$() / $(o)raw_pyrrhotite_block$()$(li)$(o)hematite_ore$() / $(o)deepslate_hematite_ore$() / $(o)hematite_block$() / $(o)raw_hematite_block$()$(li)$(o)titanomagnetite_ore$() / $(o)deepslate_titanomagnetite_ore$() / $(o)titanomagnetite_block$() / $(o)raw_titanomagnetite_block$()$(br)$(br)Plus the magnetite originals: $(o)magnetite_ore$() / $(o)deepslate_magnetite_ore$() / $(o)magnetite_block$() / $(o)raw_magnetite_block$().

Pre-charged lodestone — the heart of every advanced field-handling block (Magnetic Anchor, Magnetic Grapple, etc.). Strongly ferromagnetic on its own. Equivalent of vanilla netherite's role for magnetism: rare, focal, only used where it's structurally needed.

resolved.title: Crafting
resolved.text: 8 magnetic plates around a centre lodestone → 1 lodestone core. The plates form the dipole shell; the lodestone in the middle anchors the polarity field.

The mod's universal crafting filler — a flat plate of magnetised material that shows up in nearly every advanced recipe (Permanent Magnet, Temporary Magnet, Magnetic Anchor, Polarizer, etc.). Cheap to produce in bulk.

resolved.title: Crafting
resolved.text: 3 magnetite ingots in a horizontal row → 1 magnetic plate. Repeat freely; most setups want a stack on hand.

resolved.title: The starter ore
resolved.text: $(item)Magnetite$() (Fe$(0)3$()O$(0)4$()) is the addon's signature ore. Its main Overworld vein spans $(l)y=-48 to 80$(), with separately configurable mountain-peaks generation. Mine it with an iron pickaxe, smelt the raw ore into ingots, then craft plates and Lodestone Cores.
Drops $(l)1–2$() raw magnetite per ore (Fortune compatible). Renewable from the Magnetic Excavator.
Furnace or Blast Furnace, your choice.
Foundational crafting reagent. Most emitters need 4–8 of these.
The Lodestone Core is the 'magnet' inside every emitter — keep some on hand.

resolved.title: North and South
resolved.text: Every field, every magnetized armor piece, every ship carries a $(3)NORTH$() or $(c)SOUTH$() pole. The math is symmetric: a NORTH emitter pulls a SOUTH target the same way a SOUTH emitter pulls a NORTH one.$(br)$(br)Default convention: when a target's pole is unspecified, treat it as $(3)NORTH$(). That means a freshly-placed magnet will $(c)repel$() an untagged ship until you flip one of them.

resolved.title: The Polarity Inverter
resolved.text: Place an $(item)Polarity Inverter$() next to an emitter to flip the emitter's field. Two adjacent inverters cancel (parity).$(br)$(br)Place an inverter $(l)anywhere on a contraption$() to flip the whole ship's polarity (also parity-counted across the contraption — see Ship Polarity).
A long-range pull-only emitter. Bind it to a specific ship by sneak-right-clicking that ship while holding the anchor item.

resolved.title: Sticky binding
resolved.text: A bound anchor only pulls its target ship — other ships in range are ignored. Useful for parking spots, docking pads, and tracked-shuttle infrastructure.

A true random-number block. With a magnet placed against it, its iron domains flip chaotically and it emits a rapid, $(l)unpredictable$() stream of random redstone strengths; idle otherwise. For random lighting, casino logic, or unpredictable spawners.

A true two-ended electromagnet. While powered it emits both poles at once: NORTH from the $(l)+ facing$() end and SOUTH from the opposite end, producing a spatial gradient instead of one centered field.

resolved.title: Aiming Both Ends
resolved.text: The arrow/facing direction marks the positive end. Rotate it with a Create wrench to aim the pole pair in any of six directions. An adjacent Polarity Inverter swaps the ends; it never turns the block into a monopole. Goggles, Jade, WTHIT, and The One Probe label both ends separately.

resolved.title: Shared Controls
resolved.text: Right-click to tune the shared strength and range; there is no single-pole selector because both poles are inherent. Redstone or FE powers both ends together. Enable $(o)compat.analogRedstoneDipole$() if you want signal level 1–15 to throttle both poles together. To disable the block entirely, add $(o)"dipole_electromagnet"$() to $(o)content.disabledBlocks$().
Redstone-powered field emitter. Right-click to open the tuning GUI: pick polarity, strength, range. Active while powered.

resolved.title: GUI controls
resolved.text: The same GUI also stamps polarity onto magnetized armor and tools placed in its slot. The stamp is permanent unless cleared.$(br)$(br)$(l)Sneak + right-click an emitter with a wrench$() (anything tagged $(o)c:tools/wrench$(), including Create's) to reset every override — strength, range, polarity, ship binding — back to defaults. Plain right-click with a wrench still rotates the block.

A single-use electromagnetic bomb. Power it with redstone and it $(c)detonates$(): every magnetic emitter in a $(l)12-block radius$() goes dark for 10s and every machine/battery's stored FE is wiped, with a flash + thunderclap. Fries electronics, not terrain.
Rips ferromagnetic blocks out of the ground and yanks them to itself. Each ripped block becomes a Sable sub-level briefly. Wrench to point.

resolved.title: Fueling
resolved.text: Either feed it a redstone signal, or stash a redstone item in its internal slot (any block/dust/etc. that emits or contains redstone). Items in the slot are never consumed — presence is what matters.

Mount it on a craft and power it — it magnetically $(l)locks the ship's orientation$(), cancelling angular velocity each tick so the craft moves but won't spin, pitch, or roll. Unpowered, it rotates freely. Hold a heading or run cleanly over repulsor tracks.

Line up magnets of the $(l)same polarity$() so their faces touch and the field concentrates. Each face-adjacent same-pole magnet steps an emitter's strength tier $(l)up$() (clamped to EXTREME) — a row of aligned magnets reads as one powerful emitter. The exact mirror of the hematite dampener.

Buffers FE from cables/generators and $(l)wirelessly tops up$() every energy-storing item a nearby player carries — main inventory, armor, offhand, and Curios slots. It is opt-in because Magnetization does not itself require rechargeable gear: enable $(o)machines.inductionPadEnabled$() to reveal and activate it.

Faraday's law as a generator: a magnetic ship moving through the coil induces an EMF proportional to its speed, so the coil $(l)generates FE$() (pushed to adjacent machines) and emits a redstone pulse while the magnet passes. No fuel — pure kinetic-to-electric.
Create-kinetic-driven variant of the Electromagnet. Spin direction sets polarity; RPM scales strength. Works in contraptions.

A buried magnetic tripwire. Nearby motion — a player or mob running/jumping within $(l)8 blocks$() — shifts its $(l)magnetoresistance$() and it emits an $(l)analog redstone$() signal (stronger the closer/faster), decaying when things go still. Detects through blocks: an invisible perimeter alarm.
Always-on weak field. Right-click flips polarity. Use these to line propulsion tracks between world and ship.
The Temporary Magnet is cheaper but reverts to an Iron Block after 10 minutes. Good for short-lived propulsion segments.
Short-range $(c)repulsive$() conical field. Default range $(l)8 blocks$(). Tile across a tunnel floor for a hover-track, or line a chute to shove ships through.

Aim its marked face at a structure and power it: it scans forward, glues the connected mass into one $(l)physics craft$(), and pushes it clear. The GUI tunes strength and scan range. Fluids, unbreakable/protected blocks, and excluded materials are not captured.

resolved.title: Existing Vehicles
resolved.text: The inducer recognizes supported vehicle structures instead of duplicating them. Create: Tracks vehicles retain their Track Mount data. With Create: Coasters Simulated, only a rail-engaged train, linked cars, or a riveted body is recognized; a loose coaster cart on the ground is intentionally ignored. The coaster hook has its own $(o)compat.simulatedCoastersStructuralInducer$() toggle.

Proximity sensor for ships. Emits a redstone signal proportional to the nearest Sable sub-level within its configured detection range (8 blocks by default). Use it to gate doors, drop landing pads, or trigger lighting as a ship approaches.

resolved.title: Reading the signal
resolved.text: Signal scales from $(l)15$() at point-blank to $(l)0$() at the edge of its range. Change that range with $(o)content.magneticSwitchRange$() (1–64 blocks). The switch works while mounted on a ship and ignores its own craft, so it can detect another vessel approaching.
Directional pull along the placement axis. Hits everything in a thin cone. Great for vacuuming distant ships into a landing pad.

Magnetization's fusion machines run on a real $(l)isotope ladder$():$(br)$(li)Water → $(l)Hydrogen$() (Electrolyzer)$(li)Hydrogen → $(l)Deuterium Oxide$()$(li)Deuterium Oxide + Lithium → $(l)Tritium$()$(li)Tritium → $(l)Helium-3$()$(br)Every tier is a fluid first; tokamak fuel cells are crafted from that fluid's bucket + a frame.
$(l)Hydrogen$() is the cheap floor of the ladder — abundant (water is everywhere) and the backbone of the isotope chain, plus a low-tier thruster propellant in its own right.
$(l)Tritium$() is $(o)bred$() from Deuterium Oxide + Lithium (real lithium-6 breeding). In the tokamak it's $(l)raw power$() — the most FE/tick of any tier.

$(l)Helium-3$() is the premium endgame fuel: the $(l)longest burn$() and the $(l)highest output$() (clean direct conversion). Enrich it from Tritium, or find it rarely in $(l)deepslate / End geodes$() as Helium-3 Crystals.

resolved.title: Reading a Fuel
resolved.text: Every fuel carries its isotope mark in the corner of its icon — $(l)H$(), $(l)D$(), $(l)T$(), $(l)He³$(), $(l)Li$() — so a bucket is identifiable in a chest, a filter or a recipe list without hovering it.$(br2)Hover one and the tooltip rates it for the $(l)Fusion Thruster$(): thrust, and how long one tank lasts. Both are quoted against $(l)Deuterium Oxide$(). Defaults: H thrust ×0.7 / tank ×0.6, D ×1 / ×1, T ×1.6 / ×12.9, He³ ×2.2 / ×35.7. The numbers are read live from the config, so a retuned pack shows its own.

resolved.title: Fuel Cells
resolved.text: The three $(l)Tokamak$() cells share a marking with their fluid. Their tooltip gives FE/tick, burn seconds, and the total energy per cell measured against the Deuterium Cell.$(br2)Defaults: Deuterium $(l)2,000 FE/t$(), Tritium $(l)3,500 FE/t$() — raw power — and Helium-3, the efficient endgame with the largest total per cell.

resolved.title: Gases & TFMG
resolved.text: Hydrogen, Tritium, and Helium-3 behave as light gases when placed: they rise, spread beneath ceilings, and dissipate if they escape at the build limit. Keep them enclosed. Hydrogen and Helium-3 become bright discharges beside redstone or a powered Gas Exciter; radioactive Tritium instead radioluminesces steadily.$(br2)With Create: The Factory Must Grow installed, either mod's Hydrogen fluid and bucket can be used in compatible tanks, the Deuterium recipe, and the Fusion Thruster. Magnetization Hydrogen, Tritium, and Helium-3 also join TFMG's gas tags; Hydrogen and Tritium are flammable.
A liquid metal that melts barely above room temperature. On its own it just flows and conducts redstone like the other fluids.

Run a $(l)redstone current$() into a gallium cell that's also covered by a magnetic $(l)field$() and the $(l)Lorentz force$() kicks in — entities floating in the gallium are pushed sideways (outward under a NORTH field, inward under SOUTH), like an MHD pump. Stronger signal, stronger push. Blocks aren't moved; remove the power or the field and the current stops.

$(l)Lithium Ore$() generates from y=-32 to 72 in the Overworld, with stone and deepslate variants. It drops $(l)Raw Lithium$(), which smelts to Lithium ingots used to breed $(l)Tritium$() from Deuterium Oxide. TFMG Lithium ores, raw material, and ingots are interchangeable through common tags when that mod is installed.

Melt Lithium into $(l)Liquid Lithium$() — the best $(l)MHD working fluid$(). The MHD Jet accepts Gallium, Mixed Gallium, or Liquid Lithium; lithium gives the strongest push. TFMG Lithium may be smelted or blasted into Magnetization Lithium, and either ingot works in the melting and Tritium recipes.

Gallium with magnetite stirred in. It does $(l)both$() at once: it $(l)creeps toward magnets$() like ferrofluid, $(o)and$() it carries the gallium $(l)Lorentz entity-current$() when powered and in a field. Steel-blue tint sets it apart from plain gallium.

Hydrogen, Helium-3, Tritium, and the six ordinary noble gases share gas-like placement and rendering. Hydrogen, Helium, Neon, Tritium, and Helium-3 rise; Argon, Krypton, Xenon, and Radon settle. Dormant gas is faint. Adjacent redstone or a powered Gas Exciter illuminates connected Hydrogen, Helium-3, and noble-gas volumes, while Tritium radioluminesces continuously.

resolved.title: Finding Each Gas
resolved.text: The Air Separator produces Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, and Xenon. Rare cave pockets provide Helium and Radon. The Electrolyzer starts the fusion chain with Hydrogen; isotope processing yields Tritium and Helium-3. A Gas Detector can locate placed or naturally generated gases nearby.

resolved.title: Radon Safety
resolved.text: Radon immersion and Radon ion-thruster exhaust build harmful exposure within their configured ranges. Leave the area to recover, and use a Gas Detector to identify Radon before entering a pocket. Server owners can disable radiation effects or tune their ranges and recovery behavior.

Gallium freezes to a solid block when a $(l)cooling source$() (ice/snow/powder snow) sits next to it, and $(l)melts back$() to fluid once the cooling is gone. It still conducts redstone, so a frozen gallium bridge carries a signal. Also the storage block / crafting material for gallium gear (9 ingots).
Smelt raw gallium (or zinc/aluminium) into a $(l)gallium ingot$(). Gold-like but $(l)softer$() — low durability and quick to break.
Gallium tools, armor, and horse armor craft like gold: fast but fragile, with no attack bonus. Handy when gold's all you've got, or for the look.
A fluid bucket also doubles as a $(l)dye$(): ferrofluid → black, MR fluid → gray, gallium → light gray (four dye each).

Hold the detector to scan a 24-block spherical range for the nearest loaded fluid tagged $(o)c:gaseous$(). The needle points toward the target. Right-click while holding it to toggle the expanded, live server-authoritative readout.

resolved.title: Reading the Display
resolved.text: The HUD reports direction and state, your accumulated Radon exposure against the configured damage threshold, and whether you are exposed, recovering, or clear. While exposed it estimates the minimum distance to leave the current Radon cell or thruster-exhaust field; detected Radon otherwise shows its safe clearance. The scanner only searches loaded blocks, so an empty gas result does not rule out gas beyond its range or in unloaded terrain.

Two long Create-processing chains turn uncommon ores into engineered permanent magnets. These are progression tiers, not simple recolors: samarium–cobalt favors heat stability, while neodymium–iron–boron supplies maximum field strength.
Bastnäsite forms uncommon stone and deepslate veins. Crush either ore into Bastnäsite Concentrate, then wash it for Neodymium Oxide and occasional Boron Dust.
Monazite forms uncommon stone and deepslate veins. Crushing produces Monazite Concentrate; washing separates Samarium Oxide with a smaller Dysprosium Oxide byproduct.
Cobaltite forms in lower stone and deepslate. Crush it into Cobaltite Concentrate and wash that concentrate into Cobalt Powder for the samarium–cobalt branch.
Borax extends through lower stone and deepslate and drops Boron Dust directly, with Fortune support. Washing Bastnäsite Concentrate is a secondary boron source.
Wash Monazite Concentrate into Samarium Oxide, reduce the oxide with 250 mB of Hydrogen, then compact the resulting powder into a Samarium Ingot.
Wash Cobaltite Concentrate into Cobalt Powder and compact it into an ingot. Mix Samarium, Cobalt, and a Ferromagnetic Ingot to make Samarium–Cobalt Alloy.
Press Samarium–Cobalt Alloy into both a plate and a magnet blank. Compact the blank to sinter it; the plate is retained for the final magnet assembly.
Craft six Sintered Samarium–Cobalt pieces around two Lodestones and a Samarium–Cobalt Plate. TFMG's Polarizer provides an optional one-piece finishing route when enabled.
The samarium–cobalt magnet emits a $(l)MEDIUM$() field. Its tools and armor form a durable heat-stable tier; every worn armor piece cuts fire and lava damage by 20%, up to 80% for the full set.
Wash Bastnäsite Concentrate into Neodymium Oxide, reduce it with 250 mB of Hydrogen, and compact the resulting powder into a Neodymium Ingot.
Dysprosium Oxide is the uncommon byproduct of washing Monazite Concentrate. Reduce it with 250 mB of Hydrogen; the resulting powder stabilizes the final neodymium alloy.
Combine a Neodymium Ingot, Ferromagnetic Ingot, Boron Dust, and Dysprosium Powder to mix Neodymium–Iron–Boron Alloy.
Press Neodymium Alloy into both a plate and a magnet blank. Compact the blank to make Sintered Neodymium while retaining the plate for final assembly.
Craft six Sintered Neodymium pieces around two Lodestones and a Neodymium Alloy Plate. TFMG's Polarizer provides an optional one-piece finishing route when enabled.

The neodymium magnet emits a $(l)STRONG$() field and has the highest machine-magnet potency. Magnetized neodymium tools double personal item-pull range; a complete armor set resists 75% of field-driven movement.

All intermediates use common material tags for recipe interchange. If Create: The Factory Must Grow is installed, its polarizer can finish each sintered magnet. Rare-earth ore generation has a dedicated worldgen toggle.

Connect Create rotation to the mechanical input face selected in the GUI. By default production starts at 64 RPM and scales up to 256 RPM; both limits are configurable. Five independent tanks produce Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, and Xenon together; a full tank does not stop the others.

resolved.title: Assigning Faces
resolved.text: Open the GUI, select a gas tank or Mechanical Input, then click the exact face in the map. The shaft must use a horizontal face. Assigning an occupied face swaps the two assignments, so every gas can be piped from its own side without hidden rotation.

resolved.title: Isotope Separation
resolved.text: Install an Isotope Separation Module in the upper GUI slot, or use the module directly on the machine. It increases stress and slowly produces Helium-3 Crystals in the lower slot. Progress appears in the GUI and supported hover HUDs.

resolved.title: Air Filter
resolved.text: Four paper craft an Air Filter. It is an ingredient for the Isotope Separation Module, not a replaceable machine consumable. With their compatibility enabled, supported TFMG or Immersive Engineering plastic can substitute for the paper recipe.

resolved.title: Separation Module
resolved.text: Craft the module from a Precision Mechanism, a Tritium Cell, and two Air Filters, then install it to begin renewable Helium-3 Crystal recovery.

resolved.title: Item Fuel Intake
resolved.text: Hoppers, Create funnels/belts/arms, and other item transports can feed every item-burning machine: fusion cells into the Tokamak, magnets into the Homopolar Motor or MHD Jet, and fluid buckets into the Micro- or Fusion Thruster. Bucket machines expose the emptied bucket for extraction and recirculation. Toggle all item-fuel intake with $(o)machines.hopperFuelIntake$().

resolved.title: Fluid & FE Networks
resolved.text: Machines expose standard NeoForge fluid and energy capabilities. Pipes can fill Electrolyzer water, drain its Hydrogen, supply MHD working fluid, and feed thruster tanks. Cables can charge machines and emitters. For a Fusion Thruster, any interior block accesses the shared tank and FE storage, while every frame coil also accepts FE. For a formed Tokamak, every Reactor Core forwards fuel and FE access to the center master, and every perimeter coil exposes the shared FE output.

resolved.title: Insertion Rules
resolved.text: Each input accepts only valid fuel or fluid. Active fuel cannot be extracted, so a partially burned magnet or cell cannot be reset by automation. Machines stall safely when an output tank or container slot is full: they do not consume the next unit of input or FE until output space is available.

A powered basin that $(l)shows its water inside$(). Feed it $(l)water + FE$() and it splits out $(l)Hydrogen$() — the entry point of the fusion-fuel chain. Fill water and drain hydrogen by bucket or fluid pipe; if the hydrogen tank is full, processing pauses without consuming water or FE.

resolved.title: Coil Substitutions
resolved.text: The default recipe uses a $(l)Tokamak Confinement Coil$(). If Immersive Engineering or Create: The Factory Must Grow is installed, their compatible copper coil blocks can fill the same recipe slot. This is ingredient substitution only; the Electrolyzer still uses normal NeoForge FE and fluid capabilities.

Build an iron-golem shape out of $(l)solid gallium$() with a carved pumpkin head to cast a $(l)Gallium Golem$(). It defends like an iron golem but is $(l)weaker$() — lower health and no knockback resistance. Server owners can disable it with $(o)content.galliumGolemEnabled$(); existing golems remain but lose their gallium-specific thermal behavior.

Being soft metal, it takes extra damage in $(l)warm biomes$() and eventually $(l)melts away$() into a gallium fluid source (no drops). Killed by other means it $(l)shatters into solid gallium$(). In a cold biome it holds its shape. Repair its body with $(l)Gallium Ingots$(); iron ingots do not bind to it.

Feed FE to excite a connected volume of supported gas into its luminous state. Excitation spreads through matching connected gas blocks, with one elected exciter paying for the loaded network so duplicate machines do not multiply FE drain. A redstone signal disables it; Tritium already glows and needs no excitation.
Some addon gases exist only inside pipes and tanks. A Gas Vent converts gases described by a datapack excitation profile into a world cloud without replacing their fluid identity.
Point the outlet with a Create wrench, pipe exactly 1000 mB into any face, and leave the outlet clear. The source cell can be drained back into a compatible container.

resolved.title: Exciting the Cloud
resolved.text: Mount a powered Gas Exciter directly behind the vent or power a cloud cell with redstone. The cloud rises, sinks, or drifts according to its profile. TFMG gas support is controlled by the TFMG Gas Excitation compatibility toggle.

resolved.title: Build a Guardian
resolved.text: Build the vanilla iron-golem T shape from four matching Magnetite, Pyrrhotite, Hematite, or Titanomagnetite blocks, then place a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern. The structure is consumed and its owner is remembered. Sneak-use a Hematite Polarizer to copy its north/south setting; Hematite Golems deliberately ignore it. Server owners can independently disable each type under Content Toggles; existing golems remain but become magnetically inert.
The 100-health Magnetite Golem emits a WEAK omnidirectional field. With optional magnetite oxidation enabled it slowly weathers into a red Maghemite state and upgrades to MEDIUM strength.

The 90-health, fireproof Pyrrhotite Golem is inert while cold. Adjacent heat or a Pyrrhotite Catalyst relay drives the same ladder as the block: smouldering/fading WEAK, kindled/fire STRONG, seething/lava EXTREME.

The 110-health Hematite Golem is immovable and emits no field. Instead, every field source within four blocks loses one strength tier. Multiple Hematite Golems stack until a source is completely suppressed.

The 120-health Titanomagnetite Golem records the strongest non-Titanomagnetite field touching it, preserving polarity, shape, and axis while discarding analog overrides. It re-emits from its moving body, capped at STRONG, and cannot form a feedback loop.

resolved.title: Friendly Fields
resolved.text: A golem's own field never moves itself, its owner, or living allies on the same team. It still affects hostile magnetizable mobs, loose magnetic items, and ships. Other field sources can move Magnetite, Pyrrhotite, and Titanomagnetite Golems normally. Repair each guardian with its matching ingot; an oxidized Magnetite Golem requires Maghemite instead. Vanilla iron ingots are rejected.

A chest-slot $(l)Elytra alternative$(). Its superconducting ribbons give a permanent, fuel-free forward boost while gliding — $(l)no firework rockets$() — in daylight at any altitude by default or anywhere in the End. Higher altitude strengthens the boost; packs can optionally require daylight flight above Y=120.

resolved.title: Two-anchor stabilization
resolved.text: Pair of anchors bound to the same ship will cooperatively damp its angular velocity until it settles level. A single anchor pulls; two share the spin-bleed work.
A $(l)flat-panel$() fusion drive for airships. Bigger panels push $(l)exponentially harder$() — the mod's strongest directed thrust when fed premium fuel.

Build a vertical panel: an inner fill of $(l)Fusion Thruster$() blocks ringed by $(l)Tokamak Coils$() (the same frame the reactor uses). Minimum 3×3×1; every interior cell must share the same facing. Exhaust fires straight out of the facing panel face and pushes the ship the other way.$(br2)Right-click any interior block to open its shared GUI — fuel, coolant, FE and panel size. Vanilla and tagged coolant buckets work by hand, hopper, Create funnel, or arm; Create fluid pipes can connect through any interior or frame coil. The interior glows while firing. It only thrusts while mounted on a ship.

It burns the $(l)fusion fluids$(): Hydrogen, Deuterium Oxide, Tritium and $(l)Helium-3 (the best)$(). Better fuels hit harder $(o)and$() last longer per tank — one tank of Helium-3 outlasts even a titanomagnetite storage block in a magnet machine.$(br2)The $(l)fuel tank grows with the panel$() — each interior cell adds capacity, so bigger panels hold more. Feed buckets or piped fluid through $(l)any$() interior block; FE can enter through an interior or frame coil. It all pools in one shared tank and buffer.

resolved.title: Optional Cooling
resolved.text: An empty coolant tank preserves previous thrust, speed, FE cost, and propellant use. $(l)Water$() is baseline cooling; $(l)liquid Gallium$() is the high-efficiency option, and tagged coolants use the tagged curve. TFMG Cooling Fluid also requires $(o)compat.tfmgCoolingFluidEnabled$(). Better coolant lasts longer and raises the configured thrust, speed, FE, and fuel-efficiency bonuses. Heavy water remains a normal fuel through interiors and buckets; pipe it through a $(l)frame coil$() to select its coolant role. Capacity and base cost grow with panel size; the GUI/HUD reports Dry, Ready, or Active.

A compact Create kinetic generator powered by an installed magnet — it needs no FE. Open its GUI and insert a supported magnet; speed and stress capacity scale with magnet strength. If optional magnet consumption is enabled, the installed magnet is gradually consumed while running.

A Sable-ship electric drive that consumes FE and Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, or Radon. Each propellant changes thrust, cruise speed, fluid use, FE cost, and exhaust color. Datapacks may add fallback gases through $(o)#magnetization:ion_thruster_propellants$().

resolved.title: Propellant Profiles
resolved.text: Defaults progress from efficient, fast-cruising Helium through balanced Neon and Argon to stronger Krypton and Xenon. Radon delivers the greatest thrust but its exhaust exposes nearby living entities. Exact multipliers and costs are configurable.

resolved.title: Ship Scaling
resolved.text: Thrust impulse scales with ship mass, so one thruster gives roughly the same acceleration to a larger craft as to a small one. Add thrusters for more acceleration; their forces stack until the active gas profile's speed cap is reached. All propellants can move a small six-block ship with default settings.

A magnetic ship moving over conductive non-ferrous blocks ($(l)eddy conductors$() — copper, aluminium…) is dragged to a slow float by induced eddy currents, exactly like a magnet falling through a copper pipe. Lay a copper track to brake or gently lower a craft.

A mid/high-tier magnetohydrodynamic ship drive. It needs $(l)three$() inputs: an installed magnet, FE, and a conductive working fluid. Gallium and Mixed Gallium work; $(l)Liquid Lithium$() has the best conductivity. Magnet strength sets thrust and speed. Installed magnets are permanent by default, but can be made consumable in the Propulsion config.

A compact capillary-spike ship drive. Burns $(l)Ferrofluid$() from its 8-bucket tank plus FE; $(l)Magnetized Ferrofluid$() is also accepted and receives a configurable thrust bonus. Fill by bucket, hopper, or pipe. Stored fluid and FE appear in its GUI and supported HUD overlays.

resolved.title: The propulsion track
resolved.text: Line $(item)Permanent Magnets$() in the world with opposing magnets on a ship — the alternation produces a continuous push/pull along the track. Think a real-world maglev rail.

resolved.title: Repulsor lanes
resolved.text: $(item)Repulsor Coils$() tiled across a tunnel floor work as a one-way pusher. Cheap, no kinetic needed, and you can chain them as long as you want.
The $(l)inverse of Lenz braking$(), with insane force. Two parallel powered rails grab a ship and launch it down the channel — force grows $(l)exponentially$() with rail length.

Lay $(l)two parallel rails$() of any railgun-rail metal (copper/aluminium/brass/bronze/tin/silver/lead storage blocks), each capped by a $(l)Railgun Emitter$() facing down the track. Power both with redstone $(o)or$() FE.$(br2)A ship or magnetic mob in the channel is $(l)trapped on-rail$() and fired down it, smashing blocks in the way like the excavator — the rails and emitters are immune. More than two parallel rails dissipates the arc.$(br2)Enable $(l)Auto-Assemble$() in either emitter GUI to turn every ordinary block staged strictly between the rails into one ship, center it at launch height, and feed it into the same firing cycle.

By default the arc $(l)auto-fires$() at anything that enters. Slot a $(l)Railgun Remote$() into an emitter's GUI once to bind it and latch $(l)manual$() mode, then take it back into your hand. A target is held for boarding until you use the bound remote. One pairing covers both sibling rails and survives save/reload.

resolved.title: Remote & Safety Controls
resolved.text: Sneak-use a remote to unbind it and return that rail to automatic mode, even if the rail is unloaded, gone, or in another dimension. The tooltip reports its rail name, coordinates, dimension, length, facing, and why a fire request cannot reach it.$(br2)Block breaking and auto-assembly are shared across both emitter GUIs. Rails and emitters are always protected. Auto-assembly has no projectile-size limit by default; servers can cap the number of blocks per projectile in Propulsion config (1 for one block, 9 for a flat 3x3, or 27 for 3x3x3).

resolved.title: What ships feel
resolved.text: Every Sable sub-level (Create: Aeronautics ship) has a derived magnetic state:$(br)$(li)$(3)Polarity$() — $(3)NORTH$() by default. Each Polarity Inverter aboard flips it (parity: 1 = $(c)SOUTH$(), 2 = $(3)NORTH$() again).$(li)$(o)Susceptibility$() — baseline + per-ferrous-block + per-magnet-block bonus, capped. Iron-heavy ships respond more strongly.

resolved.title: Magnets aboard
resolved.text: $(l)Magnet blocks on the ship contribute to susceptibility only$(), never to polarity. This is deliberate: flipping a mounted electromagnet's pole for ship-to-ship combat must not accidentally invert your own ship and tear the contraption apart.$(br)$(br)Goggles, Jade, WTHIT, and TOP all surface a ship's current pole and susceptibility when you look at an emitter on it.

Mount these panels on an airship for $(l)passive, fuel-free$() forward thrust — they catch the solar wind. Build a wide one-deep wall: thrust scales with $(l)panel count$() and $(l)altitude$(). Output is full by day and uses the configured night fraction (half by default). Empty-hand right-click a panel to toggle its persistent night cutoff. A redstone signal stops the sail.

resolved.title: Fueled Thrusters
resolved.text: By default, a redstone signal stops the Micro Thruster, MHD Jet, Ion Thruster, and Fusion Thruster. Enable $(o)propulsion.allowRedstoneThrustPower$() to let redstone satisfy their FE requirement instead. Propellant, working fluid, and installed-magnet requirements still apply. Any interior or frame block can control a Fusion Thruster panel.

resolved.title: Passive Propulsion
resolved.text: A Solar Sail always stops while receiving redstone, regardless of the redstone-power setting for fueled thrusters. This provides a simple clutch for passive sail arrays without adding a GUI or consuming fuel.

Craft a $(l)Vector Core$() (titanomagnetite chip) and right-click a Repulsor Coil to install it. The coil then $(l)thrusts$() magnetic ships along its facing — a self-propelling conveyor/track — on top of its normal repulsion, up to a terminal track speed.

tokamak_ring.text_1: Fill the ring interior with Reactor Cores. This 5x5 reactor uses 16 coils and a solid 3x3 interior of 9 cores.
tokamak_ring.text_2: The center core becomes the master. Other cores forward fuel and FE; perimeter coils expose the shared FE output. This size runs at 3x capacity, generation, and output.
tokamak_ring.text_3: Pipe water, heavy water, liquid Gallium, or tagged coolant into any core or perimeter coil. Higher-quality coolant boosts output and fuel life farther.

fusion_panel.text_1: A Fusion Thruster interior sits inside a one-block Tokamak-Coil frame.
fusion_panel.text_2: Expand the interior into a solid rectangular panel; all interiors share one facing.
fusion_panel.text_3: Feed water, liquid Gallium, or tagged coolant through any interior or frame coil. Heavy water uses a frame coil for cooling; interiors keep it as fuel.

railgun_pair.text_1: Build two parallel rails with emitters facing the same direction.
railgun_pair.text_2: Both rails must reach the minimum length before an arc can launch a target. The GUI can auto-assemble every block staged between them into a centered projectile ship.

electrolyzer.text_1: Feed it water and FE; it produces hydrogen for the fusion-fuel chain.

gas_exciter.text_1: Purple markers show connected gas; pink shows excitation. One powered Gas Exciter energizes the entire connected same-gas volume.
gas_exciter.text_2: Supply FE and keep redstone off. Adjacent redstone can excite gas directly, but disables this machine.

gas_vent.text_1: Colored markers represent the gas cloud. Pipe exactly 1000 mB of a profiled addon gas into any face and leave the wrench-aimed outlet clear.
gas_vent.text_2: The source cloud keeps its fluid identity and is recoverable. An Exciter directly behind the vent can illuminate it.

air_separator.text_1: Open the GUI, select Mechanical Input, then assign one horizontal face for Create rotation.
air_separator.text_2: The default minimum is 64 RPM. Speed scales production up to the configured maximum.
air_separator.text_3: Assign the five remaining faces to Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, and Xenon; each face drains an independent tank.
air_separator.text_4: Installing an Isotope Separation Module adds slow renewable Helium-3 Crystal production.

mhd_jet.text_1: Install a magnet, point the jet with a wrench, then feed it FE and a conductive working fluid.

micro_thruster.text_1: Point the thruster with a wrench, fill its ferrofluid tank, and supply FE.

ion_thruster.text_1: White, purple, and green markers represent Helium, Xenon, and Radon. Helium favors efficiency; Xenon gives strong safe thrust; Radon is strongest but hazardous.
ion_thruster.text_2: Mount it on a ship, aim the exhaust with a wrench, then supply FE and one accepted gas propellant.

solar_sail.text_1: Mount panels on a ship and point them with a wrench; empty-hand right-click toggles each panel's night cutoff.

kinetic_coil.text_1: A passing magnetic ship induces FE and a redstone pulse in the coil.

homopolar_motor.text_1: Install a magnet and connect the Create shaft; output scales with the installed magnet.

structural_inducer.text_1: Power the inducer, point it with a wrench, and set its scan range before launching the structure ahead.

dipole_electromagnet.text_1: Power it and use a wrench to aim the separated NORTH and SOUTH pole origins.

rare_earth_magnets.text_1: Bastnäsite, Monazite, Cobaltite, and Borax supply the two staged Create-processing branches.
rare_earth_magnets.text_2: Samarium-Cobalt is the heat-stable MEDIUM tier, refined from Monazite and Cobaltite.
rare_earth_magnets.text_3: Neodymium-Iron-Boron is the strongest machine magnet and also requires Dysprosium and Boron.

steam_rails_magnetism.header: Move coupled trains with magnetic fields
steam_rails_magnetism.text_1: Steam 'n' Rails couplers share one train. A magnetic field accelerates or brakes the linked consist along its track.
steam_rails_magnetism.text_2: Structural Inducers ignore assembled train entities; disassemble a train before treating its blocks as a structure.

copycat_magnetism.text_1: A Copycats+ block inherits magnetic susceptibility from its copied material, including after contraption assembly.
copycat_magnetism.text_2: Create goggles report whether the stored material is ferromagnetic, diamagnetic, excluded, or nonmagnetic.

findings.claim: A center Lodestone Core, four magnetite ingots, and four iron ingots produce three Ferromagnetic Ingots.
findings.correction: The shipping recipe is eight Iron Ingots around a vanilla Lodestone, yielding eight Ferromagnetic Ingots. The spotlight also incorrectly describes magnetite as an ingredient. Keep the separate meteorite shortcut, which is correct.

findings.claim: Three magnetite ingots in a row produce one Magnetic Plate.
findings.correction: Three c:ingots/magnetic_alloy in a row produce three plates. The default local ingredient is Ferromagnetic Ingot; Magnetite Ingot is not in that tag. This disagrees with the actual recipe page in the same manual.

findings.claim: Eight Magnetic Plates surround one Lodestone.
findings.correction: Use PLP / LFL / PLP: four magnetic-alloy plates at the corners, four vanilla Lodestones on the edges, and one magnetic-alloy ingot in the center. The meteorite-fragment entry repeats the obsolete eight-plate comparison.

findings.claim: One Meteorite Fragment is cradled in four Raw Magnetite.
findings.correction: The shipping pattern is " F " / "RFR" / " R ": two fragments and three Raw Magnetite. Confirm which recipe is intended before changing the implementation; the page should match the shipping recipe in the meantime.

findings.claim: The depicted NORTH-facing Fusion Thruster is a valid framed panel.
findings.correction: The scene places the frame in the X/Z plane at y=1, but NORTH requires an X/Y frame at constant Z. It therefore lacks required above/below coils and cannot form. Build the scene perpendicular to FACING and validate its world with FusionThrusterPanel.validate. The scene also tells readers to expand the panel without actually expanding it.

findings.claim: Sneak-right-click a ship while holding an anchor to bind it.
findings.correction: A powered placed anchor automatically binds the closest eligible ship when unbound. Sneak-wrench the placed anchor to release its binding. There is no described item-to-ship binding gesture in the anchor item/block path.

findings.claim: Shift-right-click creates an entity-locked Field Compass variant.
findings.correction: FieldCompassItem has no use override or entity-lock component. It is a passive active-field indicator. Remove the nonexistent mode; describe the current HUD and Curios behavior instead.

findings.claim: Installing a Vector Core thrusts ships along the Repulsor Coil facing.
findings.correction: The cone follows FACING, but the added conveyor thrust follows one of four perpendicular directions selected in the GUI. Explain both directions and the GUI cycling control.

findings.claim: EXTREME → STRONG → WEAK; WEAK is the floor.
findings.correction: The enum has MEDIUM between STRONG and WEAK, and stepDown clamps at NONE. Correct the ladder to EXTREME → STRONG → MEDIUM → WEAK → NONE and explain complete suppression.

evidence.match: final int dampened = Math.max(0, base.ordinal() - count);

findings.claim: Each adjacent same-pole magnet raises the tier by one.
findings.correction: The implementation groups neighbors: one or two aligned neighbors give +1 tier, three through six give +2; the maximum bonus is two tiers, clamped at EXTREME.

findings.claim: Plain Ferrofluid is field-immune and does not move.
findings.correction: Plain Ferrofluid grows transient tendrils toward either magnetic pole, at the configured plain-fluid interval. It emits no field itself, which is different from being immune to fields. Explain recession and the original-source restriction on bucket pickup.

findings.claim: Only a stronger later field overwrites the recorded field.
findings.correction: The block picks the strongest currently eligible nearby source and overwrites its saved record whenever one exists, even if weaker than its previous record. Explain current-source replacement, not stronger-only retention.

findings.claim: Break and replace the block to wipe its imprint.
findings.correction: Loot copies magnetization:recorded_field onto the dropped item, and placement restores it. Normal break-and-replace preserves the record. Do not promise a reset gesture that the implementation does not provide.

findings.claim: NORTH emitters pull and SOUTH emitters push.
findings.correction: For an unstamped/default NORTH wearer, NORTH repels and SOUTH attracts. Stamped armor can invert the result. The nearby Polarity chapter already states the correct rule.

evidence.match: produces force in +toSample (away from origin = repel)

findings.claim: Every fusion-fuel tier is a fluid first, converted to a cell with a frame.
